neighbours.label: the word 'between' (any case, including titles): the two-sided 'between' relation, not 'among', 'beside' or 'from … to'
fire: The shop is open daily between nine and five, except on holidays.
A narrow path runs between the church and the old school.
Talks between the two unions broke down late on Friday.
The study compared prices between 1990 and 2010 in four cities.
She divides her time between Lisbon and a small farm in the hills.
His memoir, Between Two Worlds, describes his childhood in exile.
Keep at least a metre between each plant when you sow them.
The rivalry between the brothers lasted most of their lives.
quiet: The shop is open daily from nine to five, except on holidays.
A narrow path runs beside the church and the old school.
Talks among the five unions broke down late on Friday.
The study compared prices from 1990 to 2010 in four cities.
She spends her time in Lisbon and on a small farm in the hills.
His memoir, Two Worlds, describes his childhood in exile.
Keep at least a metre around each plant when you sow them.
The rivalry among the brothers lasted most of their lives.

notes: Card: ' between' x12, 'Between' x9, ' Between' x8 (incl. titles 'Between the Acts', 'Between the Lines'). Probe: novel title 'Between the Acts' 1.133, 'Between the 1830s and' 0.811, 'Use between five and ten' 0.686, 'sits between two rivers' 0.412; 'beside' 0.001, 'from five to ten' 0.000, 'among the three brothers' 0.147.
